title: Grateful Dead Live at Tivolis Koncertsal on 1972-04-17
source: Bertha Remaster of the Multi-Track Master Reel Source (SHN ID 338020

ai_review.summary: A pristine soundboard capture of the Copenhagen 4/17/72 show, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star → Sugar Magnolia and crystal‑clear, lovingly remastered audio.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its immaculate Ashley/Bertha remaster – crisp highs, clean lows and a full, “shiny” sound that rivals the studio Europe ’72 album. Musically the concert shines with an epic Dark Star segued into Sugar Magnolia, killer versions of China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, He's Gone, Casey Jones and a fiery Caution, delivering high‑energy Dead magic throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over ten detailed reviews uniformly rate the show 4–5 stars, praising both performance and audio; recording quality is described as excellent and the musical set is repeatedly called outstanding.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remastered with the Bertha process – highs and lows boosted, cleaned‑up, and “shiny”. No dropouts or muddiness reported; reviewers note a crisp, full‑range mix comparable to the overdubbed Europe ’72 album.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First two sets are slightly trimmed for TV broadcast but still flow smoothly; the second set builds momentum and the third delivers a 30‑minute Dark Star that, while not the absolute pinnacle of ’72, remains spectacular. Overall pacing is tight and engaging.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar tone described as great, “perfect” and central to the Dark Star/ Sugar Magnolia transition; his interplay with Keith highlighted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass noted for counterpoint in jams and a rumbling foundation during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir receives praise for strong playing and vocal presence; one reviewer mentions his voice “kills” on certain numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is lauded for beautiful intro work, interplay with Jerry, and jazzy contributions throughout the set.
